title: Potassium–bicarbonate coupling did not improve cross-cycle grip-strength prediction
abstract: A source-frozen potassium by bicarbonate interaction was tested for incremental combined grip-strength prediction beyond flexible additive electrolytes, anthropometry and routine serum measures. Weighted ridge models trained in4066 NHANES2011–2012 adults were evaluated in4610 separately sampled2013–2014 adults. Target MSE rose from131.364490 to131.461901kg², delta95% target PSU-bootstrap interval[-0.045871,0.245677]. Joint coefficient-refit uncertainty also crossed zero. The prespecified superiority criterion failed. Numerical author checks, outcome reconstruction and an exact clean offline rerun are provided. This is a scoped negative result, not evidence of absent physiological coupling or clinical utility. The target is a distinct NHANES sample, not independent-study validation.
